device.category: 6-voice polyphonic analogue synthesizer with split keyboard, arpeggiator and MIDI
device.based_on: Successor to the Jupiter-8 at a lower price, 1983-85; one of the first instruments with MIDI.

sources.title: Roland Jupiter-6 Owner's Manual
sources.note: Scanned; read by OCR. Performance controls, manual section, patch writing, tape memory, external control and specifications.

sources.title: Sound On Sound, 'Roland Jupiter 6' (retro review)
sources.note: Original MIDI implementation: note on/off and patch preset changes only, permanently in omni.

sources.title: Kid Nepro and Vintage Synth Explorer notes on Jupiter-6 MIDI
sources.note: Omni at power-on, channel 1 (upper) and 2 (lower) after omni off, v6.0 ROM channel select, MIDI THRU from serial 353800.

architecture.polyphony_mode: polyphonic, 6 voices; split 4+2 or 2+4; unison and solo modes
architecture.patch_memory_note: 48 patch memories (6 banks x 8) and 32 patch presets (4 banks x 8) that store a patch or split pair with performance modes. Battery backed; tape save.
architecture.summary: Two VCOs per voice with cross modulation, two-way sync and chromatic range controls, a multimode VCF (low-pass, high-pass or band-pass), two ADSRs with key follow, a programmable LFO and a performance LFO. The keyboard can split into two patches, and five assign modes include solo-unison with detune. Arpeggiator, portamento and glissando, auto-tune, tape memory and an early MIDI interface.

modules.name: Keyboard and assigner
modules.panel_section: MEMORY PANEL: KEY MODE / ASSIGN / ARPEGGIO / GLIDE
modules.description: 61-key keyboard. KEY MODE splits or layers the voices into upper and lower patches; ASSIGN chooses how keys take voices; an arpeggiator and portamento act per section. Sends pitch CV and gates to the voices.

modules.name: LFO
modules.description: Main programmable LFO, shared by the voices, with delay.

modules.name: Performance LFO
modules.description: Second LFO for performance vibrato and growl, brought in by the LFO MOD button.

modules.name: VCO-1
modules.description: First oscillator; receives cross modulation from VCO-2.

modules.name: VCO-2
modules.description: Second oscillator; a LOW setting turns it into a low-frequency modulator for cross modulation.

modules.name: ENV-1
modules.description: ADSR with key follow and polarity; drives VCO modulation, PWM, cross mod and optionally the VCF.

modules.name: ENV-2
modules.description: ADSR with key follow; drives the VCA and optionally the VCF.

modules.name: VCA
modules.description: Shapes each voice with ENV-2, with LFO tremolo.

modules.name: Bender
modules.description: Left-right bender lever with separate VCO and VCF amounts.

modules.name: Patch memory and presets
modules.description: Patch memories, patch presets (a patch or split pair plus performance modes), manual panel, write, protect, tape memory and auto-tune.

modules.name: VCF (multimode)
modules.description: Low-pass (24 dB/oct), high-pass (24 dB/oct) or band-pass (12 dB/oct, both switches down), with resonance.

modules.name: MIDI interface
modules.description: Early MIDI: note on/off and patch preset changes in, keyboard notes out.

modules.name: Output
modules.description: Volume, unbalanced and balanced outputs, headphones; foot volume control.

behaviours.name: Key modes
behaviours.rule: WHOLE plays one patch on all six voices. SPLIT-1 gives 4 voices to the lower section and 2 to the upper; SPLIT-2 the reverse. Each section has its own patch, assign mode, arpeggio, glide, hold and bender settings. Hold a SPLIT button and press a key to move the split point (not stored). BALANCE mixes the sections.

behaviours.name: Assign modes
behaviours.rule: SOLO: one voice, last-note priority. UNISON: voices shared across held keys (1 key 6 voices, 2 keys 3 each, 3 keys 2 each, 4-6 keys 1 each), with DETUNE. SOLO UNISON (SOLO and UNISON together): all voices on one key. POLY-1: one voice per key, natural releases; suits piano-like sounds. POLY-2: only the last notes keep their releases; suits glide.

behaviours.name: Arpeggio
behaviours.rule: Plays held notes in key order over 1-4 octaves: UP, DOWN, U&D (press UP then DOWN) or D&U (DOWN then UP). Mode and range per section in split; rate is shared. Repeats only while keys are held unless HOLD is on. An ASSIGN button stops it. ARPEGGIO CLOCK IN takes one step per pulse.

behaviours.name: Patch presets
behaviours.rule: 32 presets store a patch (or split pair) with key mode, assign, arpeggio, glide, hold and bender settings. With PATCH PRESET on, the BANK and NUMBER buttons select presets instead of memories. PATCH SHIFT steps through 1-8 in the bank.

behaviours.name: Editing
behaviours.rule: Moving any manual control edits the current patch live without overwriting it; WRITE with MEMORY PROTECT off stores it.

behaviours.name: Cross modulation and sync
behaviours.rule: VCO-2 modulates VCO-1's frequency at a depth set by CROSS MOD MANUAL plus ENV-1. With VCO-2 in LOW it acts as an LFO; in audio range it gives metallic, ring-mod-like tones. SYNC locks either VCO to the other.

behaviours.name: Performance controls
behaviours.rule: The bender moves pitch (selected VCOs) and cutoff by the BEND amounts; WIDE gives over 3 octaves on the VCOs. LFO MOD brings in a sine LFO-2 at RATE, rising over RISE TIME. Neither is sent or received over MIDI.

behaviours.name: Auto tune
behaviours.rule: All 12 VCOs are tuned at power-on and whenever AUTO TUNE is pressed.

midi.channel_note: Omni on at power-up; after poly on / omni off, channel 1 (upper) and channel 2 (lower in split). v6.0 ROM adds channel selection.
midi.note: No SysEx, bender or modulation over MIDI. From secondary sources; the manual only mentions the DIN IN/OUT.

source_inconsistencies: LFO-1 DELAY TIME is about 2.5 s at 10 in the text but 0 to 2 s in the specifications.
The specifications list three VCO-1 waveform symbols, but the panel diagram shows four VCO-1 waveform switches (triangle, sawtooth, pulse, square).
The OCR of the envelope attack maximum reads 18 s; the scan is unclear and it may be 15 s.

modelling_gaps.detail: Taken from reviews and forums, not the manual. Later ROMs and the Europa and Tauntek upgrades change it substantially.
Voices are modelled once; split and unison voice counts are behaviours, not duplicated modules.
